extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, newsroom staff and informed readers
extracted.subtask_description: Issuing clear corrections and clarifications for previously published news posts: identifying the original error, supplying the accurate information, and explaining the nature of the mistake. This guidance covers factual fixes (names, dates, stats), attribution, captions, labels (Correction vs Clarification), and transparency about updates or corrections to earlier corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct spelling of personal and organization names
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure personal names and organization names are spelled correctly in text and headlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples on page: "This post originally misspelled LexisNexis as LexusNexis."; "The original version of the article also misspelled Joseph Rago’s name."; "Andrew Breitbart’s name was misspelled in the original version of this post." Anti-pattern: publishing names with typographical or transposition errors; remedy: publish correction that identifies the misspelling and provides the correct spelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate identification of titles, roles and affiliations
rubrics_metrics.description: Correctly state people's job titles, institutional affiliations, and roles (e.g., ombudsman, editor, producer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: "Michael Getler was incorrectly identified as NPR’s ombudsman"; "Lila King was an iReport producer. Her correct title is participation director of CNN.com." Avoid misrepresenting someone’s position; issue a correction clarifying the accurate title and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise factual data (dates, numbers, statistics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report quantitative facts (counts, percentages, dates, traffic numbers, subscriber totals) accurately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: "The original version of this post misstated Media General’s total revenue."; "This post originally said the 454,000 digital subscribers encompasses all of The New York Times Co.’s websites, but it’s only for The New York Times and International Herald Tribune." Anti-patterns: mixing up units (percent vs percentage points), wrong totals; correction should state the erroneous claim and the corrected figure or interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate description of events and contexts (quotes, paraphrase context)
rubrics_metrics.description: Convey quotes, their context, and paraphrases accurately; don't change the intended meaning when summarizing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: "This post originally misstated the context of Pruitt's comment... He said that in response to a question about cost-cutting; this post originally said the question was about cost-cutting and transformation."; "The original version mischaracterized an exchange between Murray Weiss and a source." When a paraphrase altered meaning, publish a correction explaining original phrasing and corrected context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct attribution and sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute facts and quotes to the correct sources, and accurately describe where a quote or piece of information came from.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: "The original version of this post said the quote from Carl Elliott had come from JimRomenesko’s site. In fact, Romenesko was quoting the post by Retraction Watch." Anti-pattern: attributing material to the wrong person/site; correction should state the original misattribution and the correct source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy in photographic captions and crediting
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign correct captions, photographer credits, and descriptions for images, and avoid misattributing or misdescribing photos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: "The photo taken by Joao Silva was misattributed and had an incorrect caption."; "This post originally said the World was paying Fancher (not the library) for the photos." Corrections should identify the caption/credit error and provide the accurate attribution or caption text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct reporting of legal and status details (arrests, lawsuits, criminal records)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report legal statuses, arrests, ongoing adjudications, and litigation positions precisely, avoiding exaggeration or misstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: "This post originally stated that Cover was arrested, but he was only threatened with arrest."; "This post originally misrepresented his criminal record... one of which is still under adjudication." Anti-pattern: misstating whether someone was arrested, convicted, or merely alleged; corrections must clarify the precise legal status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy in organization names and corporate details
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the correct names and descriptions for companies, media organizations, and corporate groups (including memberships and divisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: "This post originally misidentified Cox Media Group."; "This post originally stated that The Palm Beach Post as a Tribune newspaper; it is part of the Cox Media Group." When organizational identity was wrong, correct the record and note the earlier misidentification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correctness of charts, legends and data visualizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure charts, legends and accompanying captions correctly describe the data and axes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: "The legend in the chart of NYTimes app downloads originally reversed the dates. The green bars are the week ending Oct. 9, the blue bars are the week ending Oct. 16." Correction should explicitly state what was misrepresented in the graphic and present the accurate mapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish between Corrections and Clarifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Label updates appropriately as 'Correction' when facts were wrong and 'Clarification' when wording needed explanation but facts were not incorrect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: the page uses both labels ("Correction:" and "Clarification:") and sometimes explains why the change is a clarification (e.g., wording implied something incorrect). Guidance: choose the right label and explain whether the change alters factual claims or simply clarifies wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about the original error (describe what was wrong)
rubrics_metrics.description: State explicitly what the original post said that was wrong, rather than only supplying the corrected information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pattern on page: each entry begins by indicating the original mistaken phrasing (e.g., "This post originally said..."), then provides the corrected statement. This transparency helps readers understand the nature of the error and the correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note when a correction amends a prior correction
rubrics_metrics.description: If a correction itself contained an error, publish a 'correction to the correction' that explains the chain of mistakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: "Correction to correction: The original version of this post correctly spelled Ars Technica. Unfortunately, in a fit of stupidity, I changed it to 'Arts Technica' ... So this is a correction to the correction." Guidance: be explicit about the sequence and apologize/clarify as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy in product/technical descriptions (apps, APIs, formats)
rubrics_metrics.description: Correctly describe product features, platform relationships, APIs, file/format categorizations and technical attributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: "This post originally stated that FactCheck.org has an API. In fact, they do not have an API for their content."; "The original version of this story mistakenly categorized the New York Times e-book as a Kindle Single." Corrections should explain the technical inaccuracy and state the correct technical fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision in geographic and publication identifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Correctly identify locations, publication bases, and regional claims (e.g., city or country of a newspaper).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: "This post originally included a caption for Público that misidentified the newspaper’s location."; "It incorrectly referred to The Beatles as the 'Fab Five' instead of the 'Fab Four.'" Corrections should set the geographic/publication record straight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correctness about procedural or organizational facts (who did what, when, how)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report accurately on processes, who made decisions, and the sequence of events inside organizations (e.g., hires, layoffs, policy implementations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: "This story originally said The Washington Post decided to investigate... After publication it was clarified that Jeff Leen says the Post learned of her story in the course of its reporting."; "The original version misstated how the Associated Press enables content sharing among its members." When procedural facts are wrong, correct the chronology or mechanism explicitly.
